clue.text: Hostess with young man stretching limits of legality

indicators.note: the two end letters stretch apart to hold the words for with and young man between them
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: with means and, as in bread with butter
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A party hostess and her toyboy pushing what the law allows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretching' signals the container: the end letters of 'legality' stretch round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who lets rooms and runs a pub is the hostess to her lodgers or drinkers.

clue.text: Liable to change

indicators.note: to change says the letters of liable are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A plain statement that something tends to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the anagram of LIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile is a scientific term for unstable, readily altering, as with a labile mood.

clue.text: Tory leader visits unsuspecting resident

indicators.note: visits means goes into, so the leader of Tory goes inside the word for unsuspecting

parts.note: naive means trusting and unsuspecting

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of the Conservatives calls on an unwitting local.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a person born and living in a place, so an inhabitant.

clue.text: Drawers learn using repetition, endlessly sketching faces

indicators.note: the faces of the words are their fronts, their first letters

explanation.surface: Artists who learn to draw by repeating sketches of faces endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawers' looks like artists, but it means things that draw people in.
explanation.definitionFit: Baits and enticements attract, pulling people towards them.

clue.text: Operation cancelled with doctor beginning to fall asleep

indicators.note: beginning says the doctor comes at the start of the answer

parts.note: a cancelled event is off

explanation.surface: Surgery called off as the doctor starts to nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation cancelled' reads as one idea, but it gives OP and OFF separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for dozing, nodding off to sleep.

clue.text: Get over junk you shouldn't have internalised

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: internalised says the word for thanks goes inside the word for junk

parts.note: to junk something is to bin it
said on receiving a gift, it is a way of saying thanks, which is TA in British slang

explanation.surface: Advice to get past rubbish food you ought not to have swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have!' is what you say on being given a present, so it stands for TA, informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to acquire or secure it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: But will she see you after this?

definitions.text: But will she see you after this?

parts.words: But will she see you after this?
parts.note: a meeting arranged between strangers, after which either may refuse to meet again; she also cannot see you beforehand

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a partner will keep seeing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see you' means meet again, and also literally see: before this meeting she has never laid eyes on you.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic meeting set up between two people who have never met, so neither has seen the other.

clue.text: A flower cutting to have in France — cheers!

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the river goes inside the French verb

parts.note: avoir is French for to have
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A cut flower to keep, given as a French goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, one that flows: the Ure, a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is informal British for goodbye, and this French farewell means the same.

clue.text: Greek character missing a knack for sexiness

parts.note: nu is the Greek letter N

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the a is taken out of the word for knack

parts.note: a knack is a skill or ability

explanation.surface: A Greek man without the gift of being attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubility is being young and sexually attractive, or of marriageable age.

clue.text: Texan can brush over preposterous hat

indicators.note: over says the brush word sits over, that is round, the other piece

parts.note: a broom is a brush for sweeping

indicators.note: preposterous means absurd, so the letters of hat are put in a crazy order

explanation.surface: A Texan's tin can used to brush off an outlandish cowboy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Can is American slang for a toilet, and 'Texan' marks the US usage; 'preposterous' is the anagram signal and 'over' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the can is the toilet, and a polite American word for that room is this one.

clue.text: Returning songbird impishly carries bit of leaf

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
carries says the phrase songbird impishly holds the letters within it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mischievous songbird flying home with a scrap of leaf for its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'carries bit of leaf' as the definition, leaving the hiding op unsignalled; 'carries' is the hidden-word indicator, so the definition is 'bit of leaf'.
explanation.definitionFit: The central vein of a leaf, running down its middle, is the part that carries and supports it.

clue.text: Essential ingredients to cook rabbit gumbo

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so the letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A recipe note on what you need to make rabbit stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gumbo' looks like the dish; it is also another name for the vegetable that thickens it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumbo is another name for the pod vegetable also called lady's fingers.

clue.text: Turn head of terminally lovesick sheep?

indicators.note: turn means change, so these letters are twisted into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A doomed lovesick soul told to look away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' shuffles T (the head of 'terminally') with LOVESICK; the question mark marks sheep as one example of farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are one kind of farm animal kept for profit, hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Dutch wants depravity, the horny fellow

parts.note: depravity is wickedness, or evil

explanation.surface: The setter Dutch confesses a taste for vice, like a randy chap.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is also the setter's own name, which makes the surface a joke at his expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is pictured with horns, so a horned fellow is a fair description of him.

clue.text: Scrap very loud sex when retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the two words together are read backwards

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Pensioners fighting over noisy lovemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a minor quarrel, the same as a petty squabble.

clue.text: See 20
Is Raab desperately trying to start being a foreign expert?

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild flailing, so the letters of is and Raab are scrambled
to start points to the first letter of trying

explanation.surface: Dominic Raab, the British politician, flailing to look like an authority on abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: ARABIS, the anagram of IS RAAB, gets T, the start of 'trying'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of Arabic language and culture is a specialist in matters from overseas.

clue.text: Assassinates duchess with steel-bladed boot

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for killing them
Kate is the Duchess of Cambridge

explanation.surface: A royal killer with a lethal blade in her boot.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Middleton was the Duchess of Cambridge, now Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot with a metal runner fixed beneath it, for gliding on frozen water.

clue.text: Rowdy gents are cut off

indicators.note: rowdy means disorderly, so the letters of gents and are are jumbled

explanation.surface: Noisy men are being refused more drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people or lose touch is to sever ties, to be cut off from others.

clue.text: About to master four-letter word usages

indicators.note: about says the four-letter word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a swear word, or cuss
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: Someone about to learn how to use swear words.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are established practices or habits, the same as traditions.

clue.text: Amazingly fit and also single but so out of touch

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishing has happened to the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fit and single, yet strangely cut off from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all of FIT, ALSO and SINGLE; 'and' and 'but so' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping away from others, as in a pandemic quarantine, leaves one cut off from contact.

clue.text: Produced wind to sound rude

indicators.note: to sound says the word for rude is said aloud and the same-sounding word entered

parts.note: blue means smutty or rude, as in blue jokes

explanation.surface: Breaking wind on purpose to come across as crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew is the past tense of blow, as a breeze or a person does when sending out a gust.

clue.text: I go by mainly old Byzantine life lessons

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so these letters are tangled
mainly means most of, so old loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone guided by old Byzantine wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes I, GO, BY and OL (old without its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons in the science of living things, as taught in school.

clue.text: I have to open some booze to concede defeat

indicators.note: to open means to break into, so the contraction goes inside the drink

parts.note: gin is one kind of booze
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Cracking open a bottle to drown one's sorrows after losing.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or yield is to admit defeat.

clue.text: Sound like an ass welcoming foreign visitor to shop

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the donkey's noise holds the visitor

parts.note: a donkey's cry is a bray
ET is the film alien, a visitor from another world

explanation.surface: A braying donkey greeting a foreign tourist in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a store; it is a British verb meaning to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone, in British slang, is to grass on them to the police.

clue.text: A little hairy spider brought about a state of turmoil

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says only a small part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A small furry spider stirring up chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRYS sits in 'hAIRY Spider' and is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This Middle Eastern country has been torn by civil war, a nation in upheaval.

clue.text: Appear to enjoy drinking a double

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the two words together hold the a

parts.note: to look is to appear, as in look tired
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Seeming to like a drink and ordering a double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' looks like a measure of spirits; it is a person who closely resembles another.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is someone who resembles another person closely, such as a body double.

clue.text: Barely rate jerk in Upper Chamber

indicators.note: barely means stripped bare, so rate loses its outer letters

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: Someone giving a poor score to an idiot in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper Chamber' suggests Parliament's upper house; it is a room at the top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A room directly under the roof is the highest room of a house.

clue.text: Sympathetic lady in Papuan attire stripped regularly

indicators.note: stripped regularly means every other letter is removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A kind woman wearing traditional dress from Papua New Guinea, minus some of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt-like older woman is a kindly figure, as in the BBC's nickname of Auntie.

clue.text: Spooner's to use motivational tactic getting a drink in America

indicators.note: Spooner's says the first sounds of two words are swapped, after Rev. Spooner

parts.note: to boot is to kick, here the motivating act
the rear is where the kick is aimed, giving a kick up the backside

explanation.surface: A coach's pep talk method and a fizzy American soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To use motivational tactic' is to boot the rear, a kick up the backside; swap the opening sounds of BOOT REAR and it sounds like the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with sassafras, popular in the United States.

clue.text: Go green in a weird way and articulate why

indicators.note: in a weird way says the letters of green are rearranged
articulate means spoken, so the word why is said aloud as a letter

parts.note: said aloud, why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone told to adopt green policies oddly and explain the reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means get-up-and-go, vigour or drive, as in full of go.

clue.text: Beauty to behold by the outskirts of Caerphilly

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it, to behold it
the outskirts of the town are its first and last letters, C and Y, read as a phrase

explanation.surface: A lovely sight just outside Caerphilly, a town in South Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Caerphilly are literally C and Y, and that phrase joins up into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for someone or something pleasing to look at but with little substance.
